title: Amendment-aware implementation plans via moe.amend_plan_step
description: Objective: architects/governors can amend a single plan step in place (ImplementationStep.amendments[] + activeAmendmentId) without a full re-plan, and complete_step echoes the effective amended description so workers following an amendment do not look like plan drift. Deliverable: schema fields + new tool moe.amend_plan_step (role-gated architect/governor, registered in getTools()) + effective-description echo in completeStep.ts. NOT in scope: amendment approval flows. Spec: item #1 in tag archive/governance-plane-v2. Verification command: npx vitest run src/tools/amendPlanStep.test.ts src/tools/completeStep.test.ts
definitionOfDone: moe.amend_plan_step appends an amendment and sets activeAmendmentId on the target step; non-architect/governor callers are rejected
Amending a COMPLETED step is rejected
complete_step response echoes the effective (amended) description when an amendment is active
Tool is registered in getTools() and documented in docs/MCP_SERVER.md
npx vitest run src/tools/amendPlanStep.test.ts src/tools/completeStep.test.ts passes

implementationPlan.description: Define the amendment shape in `packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts`. Add `export interface StepAmendment { amendmentId: string; description: string; reason: string; amendedBy: string; amendedAt: string; }` above `ImplementationStep`, then add `amendments?: StepAmendment[];` and `activeAmendmentId?: string;` to `ImplementationStep`. Doc-comment the contract precisely: `description` is the FULL replacement text for the step (not a delta); `activeAmendmentId` names which entry is currently in force; the original `description` field is never mutated so the audit trail stays intact; and the effective description a worker must follow is `activeAmendmentId ? amendments[matching].description : description`. Note that amendments are append-only and that nothing here changes step status semantics.
implementationPlan.note: Added `StepAmendment { amendmentId, description, reason, amendedBy, amendedAt }` above ImplementationStep with the contract doc-commented: description is the FULL replacement text (not a delta), amendments are append-only, and the step's original description is never mutated so the audit trail survives. Added `amendments?: StepAmendment[]` (oldest first, absent when never amended) and `activeAmendmentId?: string` to ImplementationStep, documenting that the effective description is `activeAmendmentId ? amendments[matching].description : description`, that a dangling id degrades to the original instead of throwing, and that amending changes no step-status semantics. Also doc-commented the existing `description` field to point at effectiveStepDescription. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0.

implementationPlan.description: MANDATORY persistence fix in `packages/moe-daemon/src/state/StateManager.ts`: `sanitizeImplementationPlan` (around line 1172) rebuilds every step from an ALLOWLIST of known fields, so any `amendments`/`activeAmendmentId` written by the new tool would be silently discarded on the very same `updateTask` call that wrote them. Extend it: carry `activeAmendmentId` when it is a string, and carry `amendments` when it is an array — mapping each entry defensively (skip non-objects; require string `amendmentId` and non-empty string `description`; slice `description` to 5000 chars to match the sibling step-description cap in this same function, `reason` to 2000; default `amendedBy`/`amendedAt` to empty strings rather than dropping the entry) and capping the array at `MAX_AMENDMENTS_PER_STEP`. Error handling style must match the rest of this function: never throw on malformed input, just drop the bad entry. Pull latest main first — a sibling task is editing this same function's neighbourhood.
implementationPlan.note: Extended the sanitizeImplementationPlan allowlist (re-read fresh — a sibling task's `newFiles` branch is already in it): steps now carry `amendments` (when the incoming value is defined) and `activeAmendmentId` (when it is a string, sliced to 200). Added a private `sanitizeStepAmendments` helper matching the function's never-throw style: skips non-objects, requires a non-empty string amendmentId and a non-blank string description, slices description to 5000 (matching the sibling step-description cap so submitPlan's 10000 limit is not silently truncated here), reason to 2000, defaults amendedBy/amendedAt to '' rather than dropping the entry, and breaks at MAX_AMENDMENTS_PER_STEP. Imported StepAmendment as a type and MAX_AMENDMENTS_PER_STEP from util/planAmendments.js. Because the sanitizer needs that constant, util/planAmendments.ts (step-3's deliverable) was created in this step with its full contents — step-3 reviews it against its spec. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npx vitest run src/state` → 4 files / 140 tests passed (implementationPlan round-trips unaffected).

implementationPlan.description: Create `packages/moe-daemon/src/util/planAmendments.ts` — the one place that resolves an amended step, so the tool, complete_step and any future consumer cannot drift. Export `MAX_AMENDMENTS_PER_STEP = 10`; `nextAmendmentId(step): string` returning `amend-<count+1>` based on the existing amendments length; `effectiveStepDescription(step: Pick<ImplementationStep, 'description' | 'amendments' | 'activeAmendmentId'>): string` returning the active amendment's description when `activeAmendmentId` is set AND resolves to an entry, else the original `description` (a dangling `activeAmendmentId` degrades to the original rather than throwing — that is the error handling contract); and `activeAmendment(step): StepAmendment | null` for callers that need the metadata. Pure functions, no StateManager import.
implementationPlan.note: Reviewed util/planAmendments.ts (created in step-2 because the sanitizer needs its cap) against this step's spec — it matches: `MAX_AMENDMENTS_PER_STEP = 10`; `nextAmendmentId(step)` → `amend-<existing count + 1>`; `activeAmendment(step)` returning the matching entry or null; `effectiveStepDescription(step)` returning the active amendment's description else the original. Error-handling contract implemented as specified: a dangling activeAmendmentId, a non-array `amendments` (hand-edited .moe/ is possible), an entry whose description is not a string, and a missing description all degrade to the original text instead of throwing. Pure functions over a `Pick<ImplementationStep, 'description' | 'amendments' | 'activeAmendmentId'>`; only a type-only import from types/schema.js, so no StateManager import and no runtime cycle with the sanitizer that consumes the constant. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; helper behaviour is unit-tested in step-6's suite as planned.

implementationPlan.description: Implement `packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/amendPlanStep.ts` and register it. Tool name `moe.amend_plan_step`; inputs `taskId`, `stepId`, `description` (the full replacement text), `reason`, `workerId`; `additionalProperties: false`; required `taskId`, `stepId`, `description`, `reason`. Handler order: validate presence (`missingRequired`) and shape — `description` non-empty and ≤5000 chars, `reason` non-empty and ≤2000 chars (`invalidInput`); then the ROLE GATE, copying the pattern in `submitPlanCritique.ts`: `const role = state.getTeamForWorker(params.workerId || '')?.role;` and reject with `notAllowed('amend_plan_step', ...)` unless role is `'architect'` or `'governor'` (a missing workerId therefore fails closed); then `notFound` for a missing task or step; then reject `task.status` of `DONE`/`ARCHIVED` via `invalidState` (amending finished work is meaningless) and reject a step whose `status === 'COMPLETED'` with a message pointing at `moe.request_replan` for work that already shipped; then reject when `step.amendments.length >= MAX_AMENDMENTS_PER_STEP`, again steering to `moe.request_replan` — a step amended ten times is a re-plan wearing a disguise. Build the amendment with `nextAmendmentId`, append it, set `activeAmendmentId`, and persist the whole `implementationPlan` through `state.updateTask(task.id, { implementationPlan: nextSteps }, 'TASK_UPDATED')`. Do NOT wrap the handler in `state.runExclusive` — MCP dispatch already serializes on that mutex. Best-effort chat (each in its own try/catch, never blocking the tool): post `@<assignedWorkerId> ✏️ step <stepId> amended on <taskId>: <reason>` to general so the assigned worker's wait wakes, and the same line to the `workers` role channel. Return `{ success, taskId, stepId, amendmentId, amendmentCount, effectiveDescription, previousDescription, message }`. Finally register it in `packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/index.ts` — import `amendPlanStepTool` and add `amendPlanStepTool(state)` to the array returned by `getTools()`; an unregistered tool is invisible over MCP.
implementationPlan.note: Created tools/amendPlanStep.ts (`moe.amend_plan_step`) and registered it in getTools() — imported next to submitPlanCritiqueTool and added to the returned array, so it is visible over MCP. Handler order exactly as planned: presence checks (missingRequired) → shape/type/length checks (description non-empty ≤5000, reason non-empty ≤2000, invalidInput) → role gate via `state.getTeamForWorker(params.workerId || '')?.role` accepting only 'architect'/'governor' and failing closed on a missing workerId (notAllowed) → notFound for task/step → invalidState for DONE/ARCHIVED tasks → COMPLETED-step rejection as an INVALID_STATE MoeError whose message names moe.request_replan → amendment-cap rejection (notAllowed) also steering to request_replan. Persists via `state.updateTask(taskId, { implementationPlan: nextSteps }, 'TASK_UPDATED')` with no runExclusive (MCP dispatch already serializes). Append-only: the step's original description is untouched; the new entry is pushed and activeAmendmentId points at it. Chat is best-effort in two independent try/catch blocks, posting `@<assignedWorkerId> ✏️ step <id> amended on <task>: <reason>` to #general (the mention wakes the worker's wait) and #workers. Returns success/taskId/stepId/amendmentId/amendmentCount/effectiveDescription/previousDescription/message, reading the counts back off the persisted task so the response reflects what actually survived the sanitizer. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npx vitest run src/tools/tools.test.ts` → 181 passed (registry unaffected).

implementationPlan.description: Echo the effective description in `packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/completeStep.ts` so a worker following an amendment does not read as plan drift. Import `effectiveStepDescription` and `activeAmendment`. (1) Use the effective description of `existingStep` in the `postSystemMessage` line (`Step N completed: <effective>`) instead of the raw `description`. (2) Add to the response `effectiveDescription` (always) plus, only when an amendment is active on the completed step, `amended: { amendmentId, reason, amendedBy, amendedAt }`. (3) Use the effective description for the NEXT step too — in the returned `nextStep.description`, in both `nextAction.reason` strings, and in the `isTestStep` heuristic input — so the worker is told to do the amended work, not the superseded work. Change nothing about step-status transitions, `stepsCompleted`, metrics, the budget check or `assertWorkerOwns`/`assertContextFetched`.
implementationPlan.note: completeStep.ts now resolves amendments through util/planAmendments.js. (1) The postSystemMessage line reports `completedDescription` (the effective text) instead of the raw planned description. (2) The response always carries `effectiveDescription`, and carries an `amended: { amendmentId, reason, amendedBy, amendedAt }` block ONLY when an amendment is active — the key is absent, not false/null, on unamended steps so existing consumers see an unchanged shape. (3) The next step is resolved once into `nextDescription` and used for `nextStep.description`, both nextAction.reason strings (in-progress and pending branches) and the isTestStep heuristic input, so the worker is pointed at the amended work. Untouched: step-status transitions, stepsCompleted, metrics, the budget check, assertWorkerOwns/assertContextFetched, and the all-steps-complete chatHint. `npx tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `npx vitest run src/tools/completeStep.test.ts` → 7 passed, so the existing behaviour is unchanged (amendment-specific cases land in step-7).

implementationPlan.description: Create `packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/amendPlanStep.test.ts`. Harness: tmpdir `.moe` (including `channels`, `messages`, `teams`), TURBO project, epic, a WORKING task whose `implementationPlan` has a PENDING `step-1`, an IN_PROGRESS `step-2` and a COMPLETED `step-3`; register callers with `state.createWorker` + `state.createTeam({ name, role })` + `state.addTeamMember`. Cover: (1) an architect amends `step-1` — response carries `amendmentId: 'amend-1'`, and the RELOADED task (assert via `state.getTask`) has `implementationPlan[0].amendments.length === 1`, `activeAmendmentId === 'amend-1'`, and an UNCHANGED original `description` (this is also the regression test for the sanitizer allowlist — if the fields vanish, the sanitizer was not extended); (2) a governor may amend; (3) a worker-role caller and a caller with no `workerId` are both rejected with a NOT_ALLOWED error; (4) amending the COMPLETED `step-3` is rejected and the message names `moe.request_replan`; (5) a second amendment on the same step yields `amend-2` and moves `activeAmendmentId` to it while keeping both entries; (6) exceeding `MAX_AMENDMENTS_PER_STEP` is rejected; (7) unknown taskId/stepId give NOT_FOUND, and a DONE task is rejected; (8) empty or oversized `description`/`reason` give INVALID_INPUT; (9) error handling — with `postToGeneral` stubbed to reject, the amendment still persists and the tool still resolves. Also unit-test the helpers imported from `util/planAmendments.js` here: effective description with no amendments, with an active one, and with a dangling `activeAmendmentId` (falls back to the original, does not throw).
implementationPlan.note: Created src/tools/amendPlanStep.test.ts — 16 cases. Harness: tmpdir .moe (epics/tasks/workers/proposals/teams/channels/messages), TURBO project, epic, WORKING task assigned to worker-1 with a PENDING step-1, IN_PROGRESS step-2 and COMPLETED step-3; callers registered via createWorker + createTeam/addTeamMember. Coverage: registry check (getTools() contains moe.amend_plan_step); architect amend asserted by RE-READING through state.getTask (amendments length, activeAmendmentId, amendedBy/amendedAt, unchanged original description, unchanged status, untouched sibling step) — this is the sanitizer-allowlist regression test; governor may amend; worker-role, absent-workerId and unknown-worker callers all rejected NOT_ALLOWED with no mutation; COMPLETED step rejected with a message naming moe.request_replan; IN_PROGRESS step amendable without status change; second amendment yields amend-2, keeps both entries, moves activeAmendmentId, and previousDescription reports the superseded amended text; MAX_AMENDMENTS_PER_STEP exceeded is rejected and the history stays capped; unknown task/step NOT_FOUND and a DONE task rejected; missing/blank/oversized/non-string description and reason all INVALID_INPUT; amendment still persists when both chat posts reject; the general post carries the exact `@worker-1 ✏️ step step-1 amended on task-1: <reason>` mention. Plus a util/planAmendments describe block: no amendments, active amendment, dangling activeAmendmentId degrading to the original, and a hand-edited non-array amendments field. `npx vitest run src/tools/amendPlanStep.test.ts` → 16 passed. Mutation-checked the key assertion: deleting the sanitizer's amendments line fails 4 tests (4 failed/12 passed), restored and re-run green (23 passed across amendPlanStep + completeStep).

implementationPlan.note: docs/SCHEMA.md: added `amendments?`/`activeAmendmentId?` to the ImplementationStep shape, the full StepAmendment interface with its caps, and an "Amendment resolution" paragraph stating the original description is never mutated, how the effective description is computed, that a dangling activeAmendmentId degrades rather than errors, that status is unchanged, and that approval flows are out of scope. docs/MCP_SERVER.md: new moe.amend_plan_step contract (inputs, architect/governor role gate failing closed on a missing workerId, DONE/ARCHIVED and COMPLETED-step rejections pointing at moe.request_replan, the 10-amendment cap, append-only persistence, best-effort mention chat, full response shape, approval out of scope) and the moe.complete_step section extended with effectiveDescription, the conditionally-present `amended` block, and amendment-resolved nextStep/nextAction. planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Mutating `step.description` in place and stashing the old text in a history array — rejected: every consumer that already reads `description` would silently change meaning, and the audit trail would be the thing most likely to rot. Additive `amendments[] + activeAmendmentId` keeps the original immutable and makes the resolution explicit. (2) Storing amendments on the Task instead of the step — rejected: the DoD scopes them per step and step-local storage means no id-matching layer. (3) Letting an amendment also rewrite `affectedFiles` — deliberately out of scope (the DoD says description); changing the file set mid-flight would silently invalidate the plan-size counters and the collision detector. Worth a follow-up if it comes up. (4) Amending a COMPLETED step by reopening it — rejected by the DoD; the tool points at `moe.request_replan` instead.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: THE LANDMINE: `StateManager.sanitizeImplementationPlan` (~line 1172) is a strict allowlist that reconstructs every step from known fields on EVERY `updateTask`. New step fields do not persist until they are added there — an amend tool that skips this would appear to work and then lose the data on the next write. The role-gate pattern to copy is `submitPlanCritique.ts` (`state.getTeamForWorker(workerId)?.role`, `notAllowed` on mismatch, fails closed when workerId is absent). Tool handlers must NOT take the state mutex themselves — McpAdapter dispatch already serializes on it. Chat posting is best-effort everywhere: `postToGeneral`/`postToRoleChannel` are already swallow-and-continue, and a `system`-sender message with `@workerId` routes through MentionRouter's human path, which is exactly how the assigned worker gets woken. Note the pre-existing cap mismatch: `submitPlan.MAX_STEP_DESCRIPTION_CHARS` is 10000 but the sanitizer slices descriptions at 5000 — cap amendment text at 5000 so nothing is silently truncated.
planningNotes.risks: 1) Sanitizer omission is the single most likely way this task ships broken and passes a shallow test — the persistence assertion must re-read through `state.getTask`, not inspect the object handed to `updateTask`. 2) Concurrent sibling tasks are editing `submitPlan.ts`, `completeStep.ts`-adjacent code and `StateManager.ts` right now (one has already added a `newFiles` branch to the sanitizer) — pull latest main before starting and re-read the function instead of trusting a stale copy. 3) Do not let the amendment path touch step `status`; a worker mid-step must not be reset. 4) The `amended` response key must be ABSENT (not `false`/null) on unamended steps so existing consumers see an unchanged shape. 5) A dangling `activeAmendmentId` must degrade to the original description — throwing there would wedge complete_step for the whole task. 6) Register the tool in `getTools()`; an unregistered tool is invisible over MCP and every test that calls the handler directly would still pass.

DoD2: COMPLETED step -> INVALID_STATE naming moe.request_replan (tested); DONE task and the 10-amendment cap also rejected.
